text:
maria: seeing a small but consistent tail jitter on e2e perfetto traces after last week's batching heuristic change. traces show a ~30-80ms spike during the client->gateway handoff for ~0.5% of requests. attaching a link to one representative perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/ABC123 (internal)

ashwin: saw that in a couple of runs. the interesting bit is the GPU kernel timeline — there’s a gap between the gateway serialization span and the runtime kernel dispatch. looks like the batch coalescer is sometimes delaying dispatch until a full batch arrives, even when partial dispatch would finish earlier.

dana: can you paste the perfetto view with RPC spans expanded? I want to see if kv-cache hit/miss correlates.

maria: pasted a short trimmed timeline below (from perfetto flame):
```
Client send -> gateway recv -> serialize (2-4ms) -> gateway enqueue -> coalescer wait (+50ms) -> runtime handoff -> kernel launch -> decode+attn
```
There are also a couple of nvprof/nsys runs where the NVTX markers show the coalescer hold.

jake: is this the same regression we saw in canary on 2026-02-12? PR #842 changed the threshold from 4->8 tokens for partial flush. If so, that might explain the extra wait.

maria: yes, PR #842 is the prime suspect. but what's odd is the KV cache log: when the coalescer waits, the subsequent batch often includes entries that miss KV and trigger a KV fetch, amplifying latency. so there may be an interaction: batching heuristic + broadcast KV misses.

perf-bot: nsys run attached: s3://redwood-perf/nsys/2148123456-run1.nsys

ashwin: quick repro command I used locally:
```
./bench_client --rate 200 --seqdist "1:0.7,128:0.3" --trace perfetto --out /tmp/t1.trace
```

dana: on the perfetto flame the gateway->runtime RPC sometimes shows a 1-2ms serialization but then an idle 40-60ms before kernel launch. what's the kernel queue depth at that time? if occupancy is low, the runtime may be waiting for a coalesced workitem.

maria: nvprof shows kernel submission spikes aligning with the dispatch — occupancy drops ~25% during the idle window. attaching the snippet of NVTX timeline: `KVFetchStart -> KVFetchEnd -> CoalescerWait -> KernelLaunch` — sometimes the KVFetch occurs after the coalescer wait, not before, meaning the batch was built assuming cached prefixes but ended up needing a fetch.

ashwin: hypothesis: batcher is computing expected KV hit-rate from recent windows; when it overestimates, it defers dispatch waiting for cached prefixes. request pattern with long-tail sequences causes cache misses on the assembled batch, causing runtime to stall to fetch keys synchronously during dispatch path.

jake: simple mitigation: change the coalescer fallback to a max-wait of 8ms for latency-sensitive routes (client-gateway handoff flagged). We tested a similar knob internally and it reduced 99.9p by ~20ms.

dana: agree, and we should add a KV preflight: when a batch is formed, proactively probe KV for prefixes that are borderline (using async prefetch). if miss rate > X then avoid waiting to coalesce.

maria: plan: (1) roll a canary that sets coalescer max-wait=8ms for the realtime route, (2) enable KV preflight probe for canary, (3) run 20k requests perfetto + nsys and compare tail. I'll open a lightweight follow-up PR with the flag.

ashwin: I’ll instrument coalescer to emit NVTX markers for wait start/end and tag batches with a kv_expectation boolean so traces can be correlated.

jake: also add a perf regression test that runs the bench_client pattern and asserts 99.9p < baseline + 30ms.

maria: thanks — I'll post updated perfetto and nsys links once canary data is in. tagging @eng-sre for rollout windows. :thumbsup:
